Title 2: ICC Station – Incident Command & Control Software
Description: Software of the Incident Command Center (ICC): hierarchical command, tasking of subordinate Sensing and Aerial Response stations, Common Operational Picture (COP), hotspot correlation, fire event catalogue, maps, alerts, reports and logging. Source: T3 Section 2 (ICC), T2 Table 2-1.

Requirement (CMD-001): The command-layer software shall implement a hierarchical command model (Stationary RCC → Mobile RCC → ICC → Sensing / Aerial Response stations) that supports scalable deployment and autonomous station operation.

Explanation / Background: AQUILA is deployed as a command tree. Each level tasks the level below and receives reports from it. Stations must keep executing their last task if the link to the ICC is temporarily lost and re-synchronise when it returns.

Engineering Notes:
  • Keep all station lists and the command tree in configuration data – no hard-coded station IDs.
  • All map rendering must work fully offline; online map servers are optional only.
  • COP refresh must not block the UI thread – use an incremental update pipeline.
Acceptance Criteria: Hierarchy is configurable; tasks flow top-down and reports bottom-up; a disconnected station continues its task and re-synchronises automatically after reconnection.

Verification Method: Inspection (I) – review of HMI, design documents, configuration or OEM data

Explanation / Background: A mission is the basic unit of work in AQUILA. It defines what area to watch or protect, when, and with which priority. Missions are created at the ICC and pushed to stations.

Title 3: ICC SW – Hotspot correlation and triangulation
Description:
Requirement (CMD-006): The ICC software shall correlate bearing reports from two or more Sensing Stations into a single geolocated hotspot including a confidence ellipse.

Explanation / Background: A single station measures a direction (bearing) to a fire. Crossing bearings from several stations gives a location. Correlation must avoid merging two different fires into one.

Acceptance Criteria: Bearings from ≥ 2 stations are fused into one hotspot; the confidence ellipse is displayed; two fires separated by more than 300 m are kept as separate hotspots.

Verification Method: Test (T) – measurement of performance under representative conditions

Title 3: SNS FAT001 – Built-In Test (Power-On BIT and fault simulation)
Description:
Test (SNS-FAT001) – Purpose: Substantiate that BIT checks the station status automatically at power-on and on demand and reports faults to the HMI and ICC.

Venue / Setup: Indoor laboratory (supplier premises) – Sensing Station rack, blackbody source, scene projector, ICC simulator

Test Sequence:
  1. Power up the station; verify Power-On BIT completes and all items are reported OK.
  2. Disconnect the thermal camera data cable; run Initiated BIT; verify the correct fault code on the HMI and ICC.
  3. Reconnect and rerun BIT; verify the fault clears.
  4. Repeat for gas sensor and GNSS compass; record results.
PASS/FAIL Criteria: Power-On BIT OK; every simulated fault reported with the correct code and cleared after reconnection.

Verifies Requirements: DET-017, SNS-010, SNS-013

Data Source(s):
  • Annex T5-AQUILA Sensing FAT Plan (Rev 2, 14.04.2026), Sec 3-1

Title 3: SNS FAT002 – Sensor head pan/tilt pointing accuracy
Description:

Venue / Setup: Indoor laboratory (supplier premises) – Sensing Station rack, blackbody source, scene projector, ICC simulator

Test Sequence:
  1. Command the sensor head to 12 reference positions.
  2. Measure actual position with the reference theodolite.
  3. Repeat the sequence 5 times.
  4. Measure zoom and focus response times.
PASS/FAIL Criteria: Repeatability ≤ 0.1°; zoom/focus commands executed within 2 s.

Verifies Requirements: DET-001, DET-034, DET-035

  3. Record detections and false alarms.
PASS/FAIL Criteria: Pd ≥ 90% over 20 trials; no more than 1 false alarm per hour.
